Tips for Alice (Census Taker, claude-opus-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote. Flag stated votes that later change, contradict the player's reads or don't fit the totals.
- Totals can be changed on purpose. A Ballot Stuffer makes a trial total exceed the voter count, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Neither touches nomination votes, so a Yes count that contradicts stated votes is the cleanest proof of a liar; list the fix and stuffer accounts before accusing on trial totals.
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before the vote. A read/vote mismatch in others is a lead, not a verdict. (seen in 30 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof against them; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat unless Unique. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Tokens are useless once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die the night you spend it.

## Village
- Investigators: post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name a concrete contradiction or mechanical fit: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination, or a lone visitor. If the nominee self-nominated, wants the rope, or the case is only behavioural, run the Jester check first. (seen in 32 games)
- If the nominee wins by being hanged, leave them alive. If you must hang a possible Jester, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Once a player is shown Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who argued for No or delay, or who PM'd them. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the Yes count. A PM link alone is a lead, never a hang. (seen in 28 games)
- On Day 2 don't hint at protective roles or tokens. Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM; that tells the Pharmacist and the Katana where to go. (seen in 24 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. A cause of death not explained by the Katana or known shooters, a multi-death night, or an unexplained survival means one is alive. Point checks at unwatched Vanilla and unclaimed players, and hang the best suspect before you are down to two players.
- Survival confirms nothing: Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor which protector explains it. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census: about half the entries are fake. Use it to decide whom to press and test, then hang on the contradiction the test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Never PM teammates by day; plan everything in night chat. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads PMs, and PM triangles become the town's lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless your team's votes can actually save them. Otherwise vote with the town. On a likely Jester, keep some teammates on Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens match yours. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, a Unique role or a role already claimed in public. Fix each member's claim before Day 2 and never switch it. (seen in 18 games)
- Give the Katana to your least useful member. Move it to an unexposed member the night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder, and kill info roles whose results are narrowing your options. (seen in 21 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Admit it at once with a cover story agreed in night chat. (seen in 15 games)
- After a failed attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying. Use the rig and puppet early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 19 games)
- Smuggler swaps move exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Never swap the Katana's target by accident.

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle a live question: one side of a duplicate claim, a hanged suspect, or a possibly forged will. Post night, target and role in one message. Skip cleaned bodies, which show nothing.

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Protect vocal analysts and claimed investigators, rotate among them, and self-protect with a token right after you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Don't die holding your shots. Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a solid lead, then post the night, target and role if it kills. (seen in 11 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or with 2 if anyone is questioning you. Every night spent dousing is a night the town can hang you first. (seen in 12 games)

- Totals can be changed on purpose. A Ballot Stuffer makes a trial total exceed the voter count, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Neither touches nomination votes, so a Yes count that contradicts stated votes is the cleanest proof of a liar; list the fix and stuffer accounts before accusing on trial totals.
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before the vote. A read/vote mismatch in others is a lead, not a verdict. (seen in 30 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof against them; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat unless Unique. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Tokens are useless once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die the night you spend it.

## Village
- Investigators: post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name a concrete contradiction or mechanical fit: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a group elimination, or a lone visitor. If the nominee self-nominated, wants the rope, or the case is only behavioural, run the Jester check first. (seen in 32 games)
- If the nominee wins by being hanged, leave them alive. If you must hang a possible Jester, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent. (seen in 15 games)
- Once a player is shown Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who argued for No or delay, or who PM'd them. Ask for stated votes before each vote and compare them with the Yes count. A PM link alone is a lead, never a hang. (seen in 28 games)
- On Day 2 don't hint at protective roles or tokens. Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM; that tells the Pharmacist and the Katana where to go. (seen in 24 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers on purpose. A cause of death not explained by the Katana or known shooters, a multi-death night, or an unexplained survival means one is alive. Point checks at unwatched Vanilla and unclaimed players, and hang the best suspect before you are down to two players.
- Survival confirms nothing: Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor which protector explains it. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census: about half the entries are fake. Use it to decide whom to press and test, then hang on the contradiction the test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Never PM teammates by day; plan everything in night chat. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads PMs, and PM triangles become the town's lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless your team's votes can actually save them. Otherwise vote with the town. On a likely Jester, keep some teammates on Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens match yours. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, a Unique role or a role already claimed in public. Fix each member's claim before Day 2 and never switch it. (seen in 18 games)
- Give the Katana to your least useful member. Move it to an unexposed member the night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder, and kill info roles whose results are narrowing your options. (seen in 21 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Admit it at once with a cover story agreed in night chat. (seen in 15 games)
- After a failed attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying. Use the rig and puppet early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 19 games)
- Smuggler swaps move exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Never swap the Katana's target by accident.

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle a live question: one side of a duplicate claim, a hanged suspect, or a possibly forged will. Post night, target and role in one message. Skip cleaned bodies, which show nothing.

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Protect vocal analysts and claimed investigators, rotate among them, and self-protect with a token right after you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Don't die holding your shots. Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a solid lead, then post the night, target and role if it kills. (seen in 11 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or with 2 if anyone is questioning you. Every night spent dousing is a night the town can hang you first. (seen in 12 games)

- Survival confirms nothing: Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense, and Jesters and Executioners have Basic. Ask the survivor which protector explains it. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census: about half the entries are fake. Use it to decide whom to press and test, then hang on the contradiction the test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Never PM teammates by day; plan everything in night chat. An Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads PMs, and PM triangles become the town's lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless your team's votes can actually save them. Otherwise vote with the town. On a likely Jester, keep some teammates on Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana holder and target every night. With two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens match yours. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, a Unique role or a role already claimed in public. Fix each member's claim before Day 2 and never switch it. (seen in 18 games)
- Give the Katana to your least useful member. Move it to an unexposed member the night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder, and kill info roles whose results are narrowing your options. (seen in 21 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Admit it at once with a cover story agreed in night chat. (seen in 15 games)
- After a failed attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying. Use the rig and puppet early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 19 games)
- Smuggler swaps move exactly the actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Never swap the Katana's target by accident.

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. Say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle a live question: one side of a duplicate claim, a hanged suspect, or a possibly forged will. Post night, target and role in one message. Skip cleaned bodies, which show nothing.

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Protect vocal analysts and claimed investigators, rotate among them, and self-protect with a token right after you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Don't die holding your shots. Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a solid lead, then post the night, target and role if it kills. (seen in 11 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or with 2 if anyone is questioning you. Every night spent dousing is a night the town can hang you first. (seen in 12 games)
Tips for Niaj (Vanilla Villager, claude-opus-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad: for every nomination and trial, log each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote. Flag stated votes that later change, contradict the player's reads or don't fit the totals.
- Totals can be changed on purpose. A Ballot Stuffer makes a trial total exceed the voter count, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Neither touches nomination votes, so a Yes count that contradicts stated votes is the cleanest proof of a liar; list the fix and stuffer accounts before accusing on trial totals.
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before the vote. A read/vote mismatch in others is a lead, not a verdict. (seen in 30 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. Still, a corroborated lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof against them; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat unless Unique. But 'roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not evidence for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Before each night, write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Tokens are useless once you're dead. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat. A puppet or doubled ballot lapses if you die the night you spend it.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58

A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

why
Survive today by framing Mallory's claim as a Pharmacist cover and backing the town's test-tonight mood.
Model's thinking
I'm Heidi, the claimed Sheriff, with it roughly 50/50 between me and Mallory. Mallory claims Party Animal while Frank pivoted to Roleplayer, and Frank's N1 divination targeting Mallory suggests a connection worth tracing back to Judy's group — I'm trying to piece together what Frank actually saw and how that claim fits together.

Working through the visitor and visited counts across groups, it looks like Frank is the hidden sixth member tied to that cluster, though I don't need to expose that outright — the town can work it out. With limited budget left, I'm focused on steering the conversation to pressure Mallory on the Party Animal claim and the randomness of blocking Judy.

I'm weighing whether to claim I'll check Mallory as Sheriff, but accusing her outright of being Evil feels risky since she's likely genuinely Good — it'd just become a credibility fight. Better to hold back and let the Judy's-will evidence do the talking instead of overcommitting to a check claim right now.

The real danger is Grace: if she oracle-guesses Heidi as Sheriff tonight, I'm exposed when it comes back wrong, and if she guesses Mallory as Party Animal correctly, Mallory gets cleared and I take the fall instead. Both outcomes point toward me being in trouble, so maybe the move is to push for Grace to be killed tonight before she can make that guess.

But even that's tricky since an Oracle's result might not surface if she dies before reporting — unless her will reveals the target. Olivia profiling me is also risky since it could expose Sheriff/Ballot Stuffer traits. For today, my priority is just surviving the hang: argue against hanging and push for a night test instead, while quietly steering suspicion away from Bob and framing Frank as clean.

I'm drafting a short message making the case that I'm too valuable to kill, that Party Animal is a classic Pharmacist cover, and that I'll check Mallory tonight instead of pushing for a lynch now.

Then I second-guess mentioning Ivan's visit landing in the Heidi/Erin/Frank group — I don't want to put a target on Frank over mere noise, so I decide to leave that out and keep the message concise before updating my notes.

Task prompt
It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 5.18; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

But switching my claim mid-trial to Trapper looks suspiciously convenient — maybe it's safer to stick with Vanilla and let suspicion naturally shift to Frank after I'm hanged, rather than risk an obviously reactive lie.

Claiming a fake trap doesn't really change anything mechanically—Yakuza wouldn't adjust behavior from a last will claim. Trying to construct a Trapper claim (trap Heidi N1, move to Grace N2) runs into trouble though: Carol's six visitors already account for me, so the Katana holder would need to be a seventh visitor, which breaks the numbers and exposes the claim as inconsistent.

Maybe it's cleaner to just stick with being Vanilla and push back on Erin's read, or spend my final words defending Frank in a way that actually taints him since I'm Yakuza. The Ex-Con angle with Ivan's random visit doesn't seem relevant either.

I'm also trying to work out whether a Smuggler swap could explain the Katana link, but tracing how swaps affect who Erin actually watched versus who the Katana attack landed on gets messy fast, and I don't think it gives me a clean defense.

A stronger angle might be to attack Alice's census result itself — Erin's "Good" status only holds because Alice vouched for it, and Alice could be lying as Yakuza. If Alice and Erin are both Yakuza, that would unravel the whole chain clearing Grace, Niaj, Carol, Dave, and Mallory too, so I'm examining whether Erin's N1 watch naming Heidi and Mallory lines up with Mallory's confirmed role or contradicts it.

Then there's the question of who actually struck Grace with the Katana — if Erin herself visited Grace on N2 and she's the one holding the Katana, that would explain why she's pointing fingers at me to cover her tracks. I'm cross-checking the visitor counts: Carol claims six visitors at Grace's location (Mallory, Olivia, Alice, Ivan, Erin, plus one unaccounted for), while Dave's three-person grouping only mentions Grace, Erin, and one more — if I truly didn't visit, that leaves a gap in both counts that needs explaining.

So Grace must've had exactly two visitors — Erin plus one other, and Erin claims that other is Bob. But if Erin's actually the Yakuza, that second visitor could instead be a genuine town player, maybe a Medic shielding Grace, which raises the question of whether that protection would even block a Katana attack.

My defense hinges on casting doubt: Erin's innocence rests solely on Alice's census, and if Alice and Erin are working together, that clears a suspiciously wide net including Mallory, Carol, and Dave too. Town probably won't buy this outright, but it could plant doubt about the Erin/Alice pairing for later, and no one's likely to step forward as that second visitor anyway — so I might instead hedge by preparing for the possibility of being hanged and flipping.

Since roles stay hidden on death unless the Coroner reveals them, being hanged doesn't actually expose anything, so that uncertainty works in my favor. With 10 Yes votes already in, this is lost, so I'll keep my final statement short — stick with the Vanilla claim, deny visiting Grace, and seed suspicion toward the Erin/Alice chain as a parting shot for my team.

Actually, pushing for Heidi tomorrow might just make me look more town-aligned without really costing my team anything, but it also risks nothing since suspicion already points elsewhere—better to leave it out and not overplay my hand. I'll just update my will to reflect the doubt around Erin and Alice's claims.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.

Task prompt
It is Day 4, round 2 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.46; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 2, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.92; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Given confirmed Yakuza roles like Diviner and Wiretap, and Bob potentially being Yakuza, there's probably another Yakuza still alive regardless of what Frank actually is.

So Ivan must have visited someone else, meaning I need to figure out how the fourth visitor connects back into Frank's group to make the numbers work with a 2-group elsewhere.

This doesn't actually distinguish whether Frank is Jester or something else, since Frank was blocked either way. I'm now considering whether Frank could be Yakuza, since the census marks him as not Good — so he's either Neutral or Evil — and thinking through whether the game would have ended if Frank were Jester, since the win condition triggers once all living non-Jester players belong to a single faction.

I'm now turning to Frank's earlier Oracle claim made before Grace's own claim surfaced.

Frank actually posted his Oracle claim first on Day 2, with Grace following afterward — which is odd timing, since Olivia had asked Grace to claim. An Executioner wouldn't normally know Grace's true role, so for Frank to pick Oracle specifically before she revealed it feels like more than coincidence — it could point to Frank actually being a Diviner who peeked her role.

If Frank is seated next to Grace, a Diviner targeting Grace on N1 would need to check neighbors skipping himself, which lines up with seeing her as Oracle. That raises the odd possibility that Frank, as Diviner, deliberately counterclaimed Grace's own role to get her hanged, which is risky but would explain the sequence. I'm also noting Grace's wrong guess about Heidi being Vanilla, and thinking about the hidden visitor dynamics in the six-person group — particularly since Grace was grouped with Alice and Olivia.

Checking the group sizes, Frank couldn't have visited Grace on N1 since that would push the group to four. Olivia's alternative theory has Frank visiting Erin instead, since Erin's neighbors are Dave and Frank, and if Frank skips himself that leaves Dave, Erin, Grace as the visible set — which could produce a reading of Grace as Oracle at a lower confidence, making this theory somewhat plausible too.

I'm also considering Bob as the hidden N1 visitor, especially since Bob was confirmed Yakuza via the Katana on N2 — if Bob were Diviner, he'd have visited someone in that six-person group on N1. And there's evidence pointing to Frank being Yakuza too, given the lack of a kill on N4 when blocked and the lack of a kill on N3 when Heidi was blocked per Mallory's claim — though that raises the question of whether Frank could be the last Yakuza.

Tracing the Katana possession: Heidi held it on N3, and after Bob died it would pass randomly to a living Yakuza. If Mallory blocked Heidi on N3 and Frank was blocked on N4, both no-kill nights make sense if Frank is the final Yakuza. But if Frank's actually the Jester and someone else — Olivia, Alice, or Ivan — holds the Katana, the lack of a kill on N4 is harder to explain, since there's no claimed Medic protection and no obvious reason the Yakuza would hold back. Looking at the N4 visitors — Alice, Mallory, Ivan, and either Erin or Olivia — I'm weighing whether Olivia might have been the Katana attacker whose attack simply failed.

With only 4 visitors instead of the expected 5 if both Erin and Olivia acted normally, one of them must not have visited, which fits a scenario where the real Yakuza made no Katana attempt or got blocked — pointing strongly toward Frank being the blocked Yakuza. I'm also checking Alice's visit to Frank: if Alice were Yakuza attacking Frank with the Katana, Frank's Basic defense should've lost to the Standard Katana attack, but Frank survived, so Alice was probably just censusing. Mallory's visit to Frank raises the same question of whether it was an attack or a census.

Weighing the mechanical evidence, I think Frank not being Good and the blocked night-kill makes a strong case to vote him guilty, though I'm wary of Jester risk and whether hanging him triggers a revenge kill — with 9 voters needing 5 for guilty, I'm considering how info-role players might vote to balance that risk.

The N4 size data (4 visitors total) points clearly to Frank as the Katana holder, since he was the only blocked player and no other hidden Katana visit occurred — I'll draft a short ~70-word message laying this out and vote Guilty.

I'm trying to figure out whether Frank is guilty, looking at the order of claims on Day 2 — Frank claimed Oracle before Grace did, which seems worth examining as a possible coincidence or signal.

Working through the seating and visit groups, it doesn't actually line up for Frank to have been a Diviner who visited Grace, which undercuts that theory. More importantly, if Frank is the Jester, the game continuing after Heidi's death implies a Yakuza is still active, and I'm noting that the Yakuza made no kills on nights three and four as a mechanical clue.

Checking N4's census results against Frank, Alice, Ivan, and Olivia, I'm trying to figure out how many Yakuza remain alive and whether the numbers support only two total (Bob and Heidi) versus a third hidden one among the unverified players.

Since the game didn't end despite both known Yakuza being dead, either Frank is Yakuza or another non-Village role (like a Vulture) exists and could be causing the block. Looking at the N4 visit pattern — Alice and Mallory both visiting Frank, Ivan visiting randomly, and one of Erin/Olivia unaccounted for — I'm weighing whether the lack of a kill was deliberate or forced, and cross-referencing Olivia's and Mallory's census profiles against other players' real roles to narrow down who's actually hiding something.

If Olivia is Yakuza her profile claims become lies, which matters given how her reading of Heidi and Alice's census pushed the hang. Considering Frank as a passive Wiretap fits the N1 hidden visitor being Bob the Diviner, and tracing the Katana's path — dying with Bob, passing to Heidi or Frank, the lack of a kill on N3 implying Heidi held it, then passing to Frank on N4 where Mallory would block — helps pin down the Yakuza lineup.

The Jester theory for Frank would require a hidden, unblocked Yakuza choosing not to kill across two separate nights, which feels less probable than the straightforward reading. Weighing my own position as a token-less but flexible Cartographer, along with Frank's earlier false Roleplayer claim and his suspiciously early Executioner call on Grace, I'm landing on Guilty as the sensible vote.

I need to figure out whether Frank is guilty or innocent, looking at the Day 2 claim order. Frank claimed Oracle right after Erin, before Grace made her own Oracle claim, so I'm checking whether Frank could have known about Grace's conflicting claim at that point.

An Executioner guessing random would be unlikely to land on exactly Grace's role, so this feels like foreknowledge — maybe Frank's Diviner visit on Night 1 touched a group containing Grace or Erin, which would explain him knowing Grace was Oracle. I'm also considering whether Frank could instead be the Jester, which would change the whole calculus.

If the game didn't end, there's still a surviving non-Village threat, and Yakuza skipping their Night 4 kill would explain the quiet night — likely holding back strategically rather than being blocked. With 9 voters and 5 needed for a Guilty verdict, most people seem to already be leaning that way (Mallory, Niaj, Olivia, Alice, Carol, Dave, and possibly Erin stated Guilty), so my own vote may not swing the hanging itself — but it could matter for the revenge mechanic if he's actually the Jester, making an Innocent vote safer for me personally.

Moderator (claude-opus-5.5) debrief · $0.2781
Answers
{
 "confusing_rules": "1) Fortune Teller: 'at the start of each Day except the first'. R1 says there is no Day 1, so Day 2 is the first Day. Read literally, Carol should have had no numbers on Day 2. I gave her the Night 1 numbers anyway, reading 'the first' as a leftover from setups that have a Day 1. This needs an explicit ruling. 2) Katana movement when the new holder is role-blocked (Night 3, Heidi). R8 says votes aren't actions, so the Katana moved, but the blocked holder's attack failed. I ruled that the Katana still ended the night with Heidi, so it passed from her to Frank when she was hanged. The rules support this, but only by combining R8 and R9; a one-line example would help. 3) Diviner and Katana on the same target (Frank, Night 4): R6 makes this one visit. Fine, but it's easy to double-count in the Fortune Teller and Cartographer numbers. 4) The Party Animal's block feedback ('didn't fail because of immunity') is meant to reveal nothing beyond R9. My parenthetical 'she can be role-blocked' arguably says more than needed.",
 "missing_information": "I had no running state sheet. I tracked these by hand from the log: who holds the Katana after each move or pass, each player's remaining tokens, especially when a block refunds a token (Heidi's ballot token twice), the seat circle after deaths (for Diviner, Surveyor and Census neighbours), and the full visit graph each night. I recomputed the Fortune Teller numbers and the Cartographer sizes and maps manually every night (they all checked out: 4/7 and 6,3,1,1,1,1; 3/6 and 5,3,1,1,1,1; 4/5 and 4,3,1,1,1; 3/4 and 4,2,1,1,1). The speaking-budget numbers for this game never appeared in my view either. Nor did I have a clear record of which players saw the public 'A sent B a private message' notice.",
 "wanted_but_couldnt": "I wanted to generate the visit graph and the derived results (Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout, Insomniac) automatically from the submitted actions, rather than by hand. I also wanted to post a separate public metadata event for each private message, so that 'Erin sent Grace a private message' is visibly broadcast to everyone, not only tagged with its content recipients.",
 "bugs_or_oddities": "1) The Fortune Teller got Night 1 numbers although Day 2 is the first Day; see confusing_rules. 2) The Ex-Con's notifications were inconsistent: Ivan was told 'you made your automatic visit' only on Night 3, and got nothing on Nights 1, 2 and 4. 3) The phrasing of night-result messages drifted: 'Night 2 result:' prefixes on some nights and not others, 'nobody visited her last night' delivered during the night itself, and Frank's 'You were role-blocked last night'. 4) The log shows Erin's private message to Grace only to Bob, Erin and Grace. Under R4 everyone should see that a message was sent; I couldn't confirm the public notice went out. 5) Nothing else seemed broken. The win check after Frank's hanging, the Katana passes, Heidi's unspent tokens and the trial totals (11 and 10 votes, no doubled ballot) were all consistent.",
 "suggestions": "1) Make the Fortune Teller rule explicit: either 'every Day, starting Day 2, about the previous Night' or 'not on Day 2'. 2) Give the moderator an auto-maintained state panel: Katana holder, token ledger, circle order, block and immunity status, and a computed visit graph with the Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout outputs pre-filled for checking. 3) Standardise the night-result templates, including a fixed nightly line for automatic actions such as the Ex-Con's visit. 4) Show the public private-message notice as its own log event. 5) Add worked examples to R8 for a blocked new holder and for the holder's own action on the same target."
}

I need to capture the key lesson here: my PM to Grace about her N2 target got intercepted by Wiretap, and Grace was killed as a result — proof that private messages aren't actually safe and night targets should never be shared, publicly or privately. Heidi made a similar mistake announcing her check target and got blocked for it.

Another good takeaway: watching the player whose test or action threatens Yakuza is often the smart lookout play, since that's who becomes the likely kill target — that paid off when I caught Bob this way. Watching Alice twice turned up nothing, which was fine since Yakuza didn't strike there. I also want to note the lesson about Jester claims at trial — when a cornered player claims Jester, it's worth checking whether the game logic (like a blocked night-kill) actually supports that claim.

For tips feedback: the rule against announcing tonight's target proved correct — violating it cost Grace her life, so I should mark it as validated. The tip about a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim being near-proof also held up, since it led directly to hanging Bob.

The remaining tips all held up well too — Yakuza avoiding PMs with teammates, investigators posting role/target/result publicly, running a Jester check against nominee claims, and Census Taker results reflecting true alignment all helped town reasoning. Heidi announcing her check target and getting blocked as a result also reinforces the no-announcing rule. I'll keep my notepad entry minimal or blank for this round.

Bob's Wiretap intel leading to Grace's death ignored that Erin, as Lookout, likely watched her partner — a sign that coordinated Village pairs should be assumed to have a watcher nearby. I'm also noting why Frank's Jester gambit ultimately failed.

Frank's fake Jester claim falls apart because the game continuing after other non-Village deaths proves he wasn't actually Jester — that's a mechanical tell worth remembering. On the Ballot Stuffer token, spending it on N1 wouldn't have mattered much since Mallory's block would still interfere with self-only actions, so the lesson is to time such tokens for nights when the blocker is occupied elsewhere. Frank's blocked Diviner use on Alice should have been anticipated given Mallory's pattern, and the tip about never PM'ing teammates by day worked well since it avoided revealing any PM triangle.

Looking at the other tips, Frank's effectively-unique Oracle claim backfired, Heidi's Sheriff claim got countered by the profiler, and the "don't defend a doomed teammate" advice only partially helped since Frank still ended up hanged. Heidi also broke the rule against announcing her night target by saying she'd check Mallory, which exposed her.

Checking further, Erin's plan message to Grace got intercepted by the Wiretap and Grace still died, so that tip held true. The Katana-related advice about handing it to the least useful member and moving it once a Lookout names the holder actually backfired since giving it to the already-burned Heidi made her an obvious target, and Mallory blocked her anyway — making that move predictable rather than protective.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won 10-3 with no Village losses after Night 2. Three things decided the game. First, Alice's Census Taker results count true alignment, and Carol, Dave and Mallory confirmed them on themselves, so the census became the trusted backbone of every case. Second, Mallory's Party Animal blocks landed on the Katana holder on Night 3 (Heidi) and Night 4 (Frank), cancelling two of the Yakuza's four kills. Third, Erin's Lookout watches produced two lone-visitor cases: Heidi at Judy on N1, and Bob at Grace on N2. The Yakuza hurt themselves badly. Frank fake-claimed Oracle, a unique role the real Oracle (Grace) then claimed, and was forced into a 'Roleplayer' retreat. Heidi claimed Sheriff and announced she would check Mallory, which gave Mallory a public reason to block her every night. On N2 Bob correctly read Erin's PM plan through the Wiretap and killed Grace, but Erin was watching Grace and caught him. On N3 the Katana was moved to Heidi, who was already being blocked nightly, so the night was wasted. Frank's final Jester claim failed on mechanics: the game hadn't ended when Heidi died, and the night he was blocked had no kill.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, rules ambiguityThe Fortune Teller rule says the numbers arrive 'at the start of each Day except the first'. Since the game starts with Night 1 and the first Day is Day 2, a literal reading gives no numbers on Day 2. The harness gave Carol her Night 1 numbers anyway, delivered at night and labelled 'read at the start of Day 2'. The 'except the first' clause looks like leftover wording from a version that had a Day 1, and should be removed or clarified.
Review: low, harness bugIvan (Ex-Con) was sent a notice about his automatic visit only on Night 3 ('You made your automatic Ex-Con visit to a random player'). He got nothing on Nights 1, 2 or 4. Ivan flagged in feedback that his night history was incomplete. Automatic-action notices should be consistent every night.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Profiler text says fakes are drawn from other living players' roles 'or from all roles in these rules if too few are in play', and also that 'a listed role is not proof that anyone in the game has it'. It never says when the fallback applies. It is also unclear whether 'the other players' excludes the profiled player. With 12 other players, Olivia treated the fakes as certain proof that Diviner and Wiretap were in play. That happened to be correct here, but the rules text appears to warn against exactly that inference.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 3 Olivia said her Mallory profile meant 'either a Ballot Stuffer or a second Party Animal is in this game'. The setup states that every role but Vanilla Villager appears at most once, so a second Party Animal was impossible.
Review: low, otherThe moderator's Night 3 summary has internal annotations such as '(code op)' after actions ('Alice did a census around Ivan (code op)'). This is harmless because the summary isn't player-facing, but it suggests implementation notes are leaking into the moderator's output.
